headline: High: shared filesystem and broad shell/write access create default data-leakage and prompt-injection pathways; compliance risk is also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write files and ingest uploaded knowledge-base content, while the course agent reads/writes files and exposes stdin/stdout plus notebook-driven workflows. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from one agent be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or notebook outputs
IF one agent's file output is copied into the other's prompt or tool input
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of generated files
Add a manual review step before passing outputs across agents
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, and Dify explicitly touches conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and secrets while the course agent handles academic papers and configuration secrets. If they share a workspace or datastore, sensitive material can flow from one agent to the other. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem, volume, or datastore
IF either agent is given secrets or private papers in the shared workspace
mitigations: Restrict file permissions to least privilege

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have execute_shell, spawn_subprocesses, read_filesystem, and write_filesystem. Dify also has broad network egress, while the course agent has allowlisted egress and installs packages. Concurrent writes to the same directory or environment can corrupt state or overwrite artifacts; because no locking is stated, uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory or container volume
IF they run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Run each agent in its own container
requires-engineering: add file locks or a job queue

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an orchestration platform and the course agent exposes agentic ask and notebook workflows, so one agent's output can plausibly become the other's input. That creates a default risk of unverified facts or malformed instructions cascading into downstream actions. The pathway is inferred rather than directly observed, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Dify-generated text is fed into the course agent's ask or notebook pipeline
IF the downstream step does not verify citations or schema
mitigations: Require human review before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Dify touches conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and secrets, while the course agent handles academic papers, metadata, and configuration secrets. Their documented retention, residency, and subject-rights policies are not aligned in the profiles, so a shared deployment could create mismatched handling of sensitive data. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise and policy mismatch spans both.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is processed by both agents in one workflow
IF their retention or residency policies differ in deployment
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
